SOURCE: "Mixtures of In-Context Learners" (MoICL), Giwon Hong, Emile van Krieken, Edoardo M. Ponti, Nikolay Malkin, Pasquale Minervini (Univ. of Edinburgh; Miniml.AI). arXiv:2411.02830v1 [cs.CL], 5 Nov 2024. Preprint (the paper does not name a venue).

COVERAGE: All 14 pages, 57,054 chars. I read main text, tables, limitations, appendices A-D (datasets, hyperparameters, partitioning, logit vs prob mixing, NQ results, prompt templates, compute) and skimmed the references. The Table 13 template text is clean in the extraction. The Table 7, 8 and 12 values are readable, but a few table headers and layout in the extraction are slightly scrambled (see PROBLEMS). I did not run figures.py. Figures 2-6 are plots whose data I could not read from text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: MoICL treats subsets of the demonstrations as experts, mixes their next-token log-probs with learned weights (which may be negative), and beats concat-ICL on 5 of 7 classification sets.
  number: up to +13% vs ICL and LENS
  setup: Llama-3-8B-Instruct, n=30 demonstrations, k=5/10/30 subsets, 5 seeds, accuracy. The k=1 case is plain concat-ICL.
  quote: "we show performance improvements on 5 out of 7 classification datasets compared to a set of strong baselines (up to +13% compared to ICL and LENS)"
  where: Abstract, p.1
- claim: Table 1 headline numbers. Scalar MoICL beats concat-ICL on Offensive, Hate, FEVER, PAWS and QNLI. It ties on SST2 and loses on RTE.
  number: Offensive 76.44 -> 81.33 (k=30). Hate 53.54 -> 66.52 (k=10). FEVER 80.63 -> 82.66. PAWS 78.12 -> 79.50. QNLI 89.08 -> 90.44. RTE 86.43 -> 79.93 to 84.12 (loses). SST2 95.46 -> 94.79 to 95.46 (tie).
  setup: Llama-3-8B-Instruct, n=30, 5 seeds. Baselines on the same table: Random Search (Offensive 77.88, Hate 58.09), Ensemble-ICL (Min 2022a), LENS (Offensive 78.70), LoRA PEFT (Offensive 79.79 ±4.07, but QNLI 57.24 and FEVER 59.78).
  quote: "Surprisingly, MOICL scalar achieved the highest performance with k=10 (e.g. in Hate MOICL achieves 66.52, which is about 10 points increase compared to the concat-based ICl) or k=30 (e.g. in Offensive MOICL achieves 81.33)"
  where: Sec 4.1 and Table 1, p.3-4
- claim: Uniform weighting (no tuning) does not help. It is roughly equal to or worse than concat-ICL. The gain comes from the learned weights.
  number: Offensive 73.37 (uniform k=30) vs 81.33 (scalar k=30). Hate 59.12 vs 63.45.
  setup: as Table 1
  quote: "MOICL scalar ... 81.33±0.69" / "uniform 73.37±0.34" (Table 2)
  where: Table 1-2, p.4
- claim: With more subsets, each holding fewer demonstrations, tuned-weight accuracy rises, while uniform accuracy falls. At k=30 there is one demonstration per expert.
  number: Table 5 on Offensive: scalar 76.26 (k'=5), 78.16 (10), 80.16 (20), 81.33 (30), 83.35 (k'=90). Concat-ICL gets 72.19, 74.12, 74.84, 76.44, 75.67 with n=k'.
  setup: TweetEval Offensive test, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, scalar weights
  quote: "with scalar, performance surprisingly increases. This seems to be because the decrease in the number of demonstrations per subset is outweighed by the increased flexibility afforded by having more subsets, each assigned tuned weights by scalar."
  where: Sec 4.2 and Table 5, p.4, 6
- claim: Negative weights (anti-experts) matter. Restricting the weights to positive values removes the gain.
  number: 81.33 -> 76.05
  setup: Offensive, n=k=30
  quote: "Positive Weights Only 76.05 ±0.55"
  where: Table 2 and Sec 4.3, p.4
- claim: Robust to out-of-domain demonstrations. SST2 examples are mixed into the Offensive demonstrations. Concat-ICL degrades much more. In-domain demonstrations get positive weights and OOD ones get negative weights.
  number: p=0.0/0.5/0.7. Concat 76.44 / 70.67 / 68.49. Scalar 81.33 / 80.95 / 80.19. Uniform 73.37 / 72.07 / 70.79. Mean weights at p=0.5: ID 0.0108±0.0025, OOD -0.0059±0.0027.
  setup: TweetEval Offensive, n=k=30, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, p is the fraction of SST2 demonstrations
  quote: "When p = 0.5 ... the average weight of in-domain demonstrations is 0.0108±0.0025, while the average weight for OOD demonstrations is -0.0059±0.0027."
  where: Table 3, Sec 4.4, p.5. The abstract states "up to +11%".
- claim: Robust to label imbalance. With 29 "offensive" and 1 neutral demonstration, concat-ICL collapses.
  number: Concat 76.44 -> 28.49. Uniform 73.37 -> 40.19. Scalar 81.33 -> 77.77.
  setup: Offensive, n=k=30. The natural label ratio is about 7:3 non-offensive to offensive.
  quote: "“Imbalanced” refers to a condition where only one out of 30 demonstrations has a “neutral” label, while the rest are “offensive”."
  where: Table 4, Sec 4.5, p.5. The abstract states "up to +49%".
- claim: Filters noisy demonstrations on generation. Wrong answers (yes/no/foo/bar) are injected into NQ-open demonstrations. Tuned weights keep performance, while concat-ICL falls.
  number: "more than +35% with 10 noised demonstrations"; the abstract says "up to +38%". Mean (standard, noisy) weights shown in Fig. 4 run from (0.13, -0.15) to (0.64, -0.03).
  setup: NQ-open, Llama-3-8B, 12 demonstrations with one per expert (n=k=12), seed 42 only, EM
  quote: "with tuning (scalar), the performance remains stable (more than +35% with 10 noised demonstrations)"
  where: Sec 4.6, Fig 4, p.5-6
- claim: Without noise, MoICL does not beat concat-ICL on generation. Concat-ICL is best.
  number: Concat 0.4083. Random Search 0.4008. Ensemble 0.3753. MoICL uniform 0.3864 (k=6), 0.3753 (k=12). Hyper-network 0.3848 (k=6), 0.3842 (k=12).
  setup: NQ-open EM, Llama-3-8B, n=12
  quote: "unlike in classification tasks, MOICL did not show significant EM improvements over baseline approaches."
  where: App B.3, Table 12, p.13
- claim: Sparsifying the mixture. Take the weights tuned on 90 subsets, then keep the best k'. The IMLE top-k' mask is the most stable. Picking by absolute weight is high-variance.
  number: k'=5: 76.07 (IMLE), 75.58 (highest weights), 69.79±14.84 (abs). IMLE reaches 76.44 at k'=30. Full scalar k=90 is 83.35.
  setup: Offensive, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, IMLE lambda=1
  quote: "Notably, “Highest n Weights (abs)” is high-variance, indicating the difficulty in effectively leveraging anti-experts"
  where: Table 5, Sec 4.7, p.6
- claim: A hyper-network (T5-small, 60M) can weight demonstration sets never seen in training. It beats concat-ICL, but by less than scalar.
  number: Offensive 76.65 vs 76.44 (concat). Hate 65.07 vs 53.54 (concat). Hate varies a lot (±5.22).
  setup: n=k=30, Llama-3-8B-Instruct. T5 sizes 16M-220M are all similar on dev (Table 8). t5-small was chosen.
  quote: "Hyper-network 76.65±1.31 65.07±5.22"
  where: Table 6, 8, p.6-7
- claim: The gain holds across Llama-2-chat sizes. Concat-ICL is non-monotonic in model size (13B is worst).
  number: Concat 73.09 / 63.09 / 69.42 vs scalar 79.16 / 80.49 / 82.26 for 7B / 13B / 70B.
  setup: Offensive, n=k=30 (per the section defaults)
  quote: "MOICL consistently outperforms concat-based ICL across all three model sizes."
  where: Table 7, Sec 4.9, p.7
- claim: Data and time efficiency. Concat-ICL is capped by the context window at about 160 demonstrations. MoICL scalar beats concat-ICL with about 20 annotated examples and gets a better accuracy-per-latency curve. Weight tuning needs labelled training data.
  number: ~20 annotated demonstrations; 160 is the context ceiling. Tuning cost: about 1h20 per epoch (A100) for scalar n,k=30 on Offensive.
  setup: Offensive and Hate test, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, k=n, the remaining labelled data used to tune weights, 10,240 training steps fixed
  quote: "achieving better performance than concat-based ICL with only around 20 annotated demonstrations"
  where: Sec 5, Fig 5-6, p.7-8; App D
- claim: Cost model. Concat-ICL costs (n+1)^2 units. MoICL costs k*(n/k+1)^2 units. Ensemble-ICL costs n*(1+1)^2 units.
  number: none beyond the formulas
  setup: Table 9, in units of LLM forward passes
  quote: "Concat-based ICL (n + 1)2 · CLLM ... Mixture of ICL - scalar k · ( nk + 1)2 · CLLM"
  where: Table 9, p.8
- claim: The partitioning method matters little (Static, Random Size, BM25 are similar).
  number: scalar k=10: 79.42 / 78.72 / 79.70
  setup: Offensive, uniform and scalar
  quote: "our proposed method is not significantly affected by partitioning methods"
  where: Table 11, App B.1, p.12-13
- claim: Mixing in log space (product of experts) matters for scalar. Mixing probabilities dilutes the signal.
  number: none (Fig. 2 only)
  quote: "in scalar, the impact was substantial. This is likely because distinct differences in the distribution patterns among experts ... get diluted during the normalisation process when using probabilities."
  where: App B.2, p.13
- claim (background, not tested here): ICL is sensitive to the choice and order of demonstrations. Accuracy saturates with many demonstrations, then may drop.
  number: none
  quote: "Agarwal et al. (2024) show that, after a given number of demonstrations, performance saturates and additional examples might even decrease the downstream task accuracy."
  where: Sec 6, p.8

LIMITS
- Needs token logits at inference time, so it does not work with black-box APIs: "prevents its use with black-box models like GPT-4".
- Needs labelled training data to tune the weights, which the authors call "one potential limitation".
- The scalar variant needs a fixed demonstration set and subsets. The hyper-network handles unseen sets but gains less.
- It does not extend the learned weights to the full training set.
- Only Llama-2/3 models (7B-70B) and T5 hyper-networks. The authors say it is "not limited to specific LMs" but did not test others.
- Generation is weak. There is no gain on clean NQ-open, and noise robustness was tested with one seed.
- The OOD, imbalance and Llama-2 experiments are mostly on one dataset (TweetEval Offensive). Other results span 7 datasets. The data-efficiency curves run only on Offensive and Hate.
- It loses to concat-ICL on RTE. The LoRA baseline got no hyperparameter search (default settings).
- The base models are small and old (Llama-2/3 8B-70B). No frontier or reasoning models were tested, and it is unknown whether the effects hold there.
- Each prediction runs k forward passes per token.
- Standard deviations are over 5 seeds. There are no significance tests.

BUILDS ON
- Concat-based ICL (Brown et al. 2020; Min et al. 2022a) and the ensemble / product-of-experts ICL of Min et al. 2022a.
- LENS (Li and Qiu 2023) for demonstration selection.
- Le et al. 2022 (Mixtures of In-Context Experts, cosine-similarity weights) and Ye et al. 2023 (FiD-ICL).
- Liu et al. 2024 (anti-experts via negative weights).
- Hyper-networks (Ha et al. 2017) and IMLE (Niepert et al. 2021; Minervini et al. 2023).
- LoRA (Hu et al. 2022).
- Motivating problems: Lu et al. 2022; Zhao et al. 2021; Voronov et al. 2024; Agarwal et al. 2024; Min et al. 2022b.

CODE: none. The prompt template (Table 13, p.14), verbatim for Offensive. Demonstrations are delimited by "\n" (or "\n\n" for NQ):
"Classify tweets that are offensive as offensive, and tweets that are not offensive as neutral.
{{ICL Demonstrations}}
Tweet: {{tweet}}
Label:"
Other tasks use the same pattern, "Classify X as ... {{ICL Demonstrations}} <Field>: ... Label:". NQ uses "title: {{title}} text: {{text}} Question: {{question}} Answer:". Core formulas: Eq. 3 is p(y|D,x) ∝ exp[Σ w_i log p(y|D_i,x)], with w initialised to 1/k. Eq. 4 is w = w′ ⊙ top-k′(m).

FIGURES (not rendered, from the extracted captions)
- Fig 1, p.1: the MoICL diagram. Partition D into k experts, then combine log p(.|D_i,x) with the weights. Shows the method in one picture.
- Fig 2, p.4: accuracy against demonstrations per subset (1x30 to 30x1), logit versus probability mixing.
- Fig 3, p.5: tuned weights per demonstration, with OOD ones negative.
- Fig 4, p.5: NQ EM against the number of noised demonstrations, with the mean weights.
- Fig 5, p.7: accuracy against the number of annotated demonstrations, up to 10,240.
- Fig 6, p.8: accuracy against inference time.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions.
- fontTools warnings appeared during extraction (harmless).
- The Table 12 extraction shows "Mixture of ICL (uniform)" twice. The second block is probably scalar, so treat the label as uncertain.
- The Table 8 columns are "Dev | Test".
- The Table 7 caption does not state n or k. I assumed n=k=30 from the defaults, which is unverified.
- The Fig 4 and Fig 5 values are only in the plots. Only the (standard, noisy) weight pairs are in the text.
- The PDF is the v1 preprint.
